title: Come to Me: Rest for the Weary Soul
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Context of Rejection and Revelation
subpoints: Matthew 11 marks a shift toward increased rejection of Jesus by the crowds and religious leaders.
Jesus rebukes Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum for witnessing miracles but refusing to repent.
In response to unbelief, Jesus praises the Father for hiding truth from the 'wise and prudent' and revealing it to 'babes'.

outline.title: The Sovereignty of Divine Revelation
subpoints: God sovereignly reveals Himself; knowledge of the Father and Son is a gift, not a product of human intellect.
The 'wise and prudent' (religious elites) failed to recognize the Messiah due to self-reliance.
The 'babes' (humble, simple believers) received the truth because they were willing to be taught.

outline.title: The Sincere Invitation to All
subpoints: Jesus extends a genuine invitation to 'all you who labor and are heavy laden.'
The doctrine of election and the free offer of the gospel stand side by side.
Christ alone can provide true rest, as He is the only one who can reveal the Father.

outline.title: The Yoke of Christ: Submission over Self-Effort
subpoints: Jesus offers Himself, not advice or time-management techniques, to the weary.
True rest is found in submission to the Savior, not in religious performance or legalism.
Christ’s yoke is easy and His burden is light because it is shared with Him, not borne alone.

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro addresses the universal human condition of exhaustion, anxiety, and spiritual weariness. Drawing from Matthew 11:25-30, he highlights the contrast between the 'wise and prudent' who rejected Jesus through self-reliance and the 'babes' who received Him through humility. The message emphasizes that divine revelation is a sovereign act of God, where truth is hidden from those who trust in their own understanding and revealed to those who approach God with childlike dependence.

The core of the sermon is the sincere invitation of Christ to all who are burdened. Pastor Lyro clarifies that Jesus does not offer mere advice or techniques for managing life's stresses but offers Himself as the source of rest. This invitation exposes both the unbeliever's reliance on self-effort to be right with God and the believer's residual legalism. True rest is not found in religious observance, psychological insight, or worldly success, but exclusively in submission to the Lord Jesus Christ.

The sermon concludes by affirming that while judgment is real, as seen in the warnings to the cities of Galilee, Jesus graciously calls sinners to redemption. The 'yoke' of Christ is described as easy and light because it involves learning from His gentle and lowly heart, allowing believers to lay their heavy burdens at the foot of the cross and find peace for their souls.
